text: AgiBot X2 Ultra, the same model files for every track.
Two apparatuses: ours (the IEEE loco-manipulation apparatus, from the CAD) and the NIST one. Neither goes into training as a whole; only separate, re-arranged parts may.
Door, 4x4 stepovers, buttons 1-2, crossing ramps, buttons 3-4, wall, stairs, landing, button 5.
One robot, one attempt at the whole route, commands produced from the waypoints only. No reference motion replay.

Reaches every waypoint within 180 s, both 4x4s stepped over, no fall, never off the course, and a strict 1 s stand at each station (feet loaded, nearly still, upright afterwards). Also reported per section, with falls, stalls and where.
status: Set (time limit 180 s; strict stand confirmed by you)

text: At least 200 trials per checkpoint with randomised start pose and physics, same seeds for every track. A 99% claim needs at least 500 trials; the final claim uses 1,000.
Scores are measured in MuJoCo on CPU, the common cross-check, with the gains each policy trained with. A track's number counts only if it holds there.

Feet collide with planes and boxes (floor, steps, ramp slabs trimmed to the scanned edge, 4x4s); the height field is drawn and scanned only. Results on the earlier height-field floor are marked 'old floor'.
Flat gate (walk, stop and stand, turn in place, turn and return; 50 each), ACP's hold-out gate, then five station legs of 50 trials; the full route (200 trials) only when every leg reaches 45 of 50.
status: Pass mark 45 of 50 waiting for your yes

text: Each trial is checked for trapped feet, clamped limbs, joints past their range and unphysical contacts; a failure counts against a policy only when the physics around it is plausible.
